example_german: Ich komme nicht, weil ich krank bin.
example_english: I'm not coming because I'm sick.
wordorder_rule: Verb to end. If the subordinate clause comes first, invert main clause: "Weil ich krank bin, komme ich nicht."

example_german: Wenn es regnet, bleibe ich zu Hause.
example_english: If it rains, I stay home.
wordorder_rule: Use for repeated past events and conditions. For a single past event, use "als".

example_german: Obwohl es regnet, gehe ich raus.
example_english: Although it's raining, I'm going out.

example_german: Da er krank ist, kommt er nicht.
example_english: Since he's sick, he's not coming.
wordorder_rule: More formal than "weil" — common in written German and clause-initial position.

example_german: Als ich jung war, spielte ich Fußball.
example_english: When I was young, I played football.
wordorder_rule: Only for single past events. For repeated/conditional, use "wenn".

example_german: Ich lerne, damit ich die Prüfung bestehe.
example_english: I study so that I pass the exam.

example_german: Ich weiß nicht, ob er kommt.
example_english: I don't know whether he's coming.

example_german: Bevor ich gehe, trinke ich Kaffee.
example_english: Before I go, I drink coffee.

example_german: Nachdem ich gegessen hatte, schlief ich.
example_english: After I had eaten, I slept.
wordorder_rule: Often uses Plusquamperfekt (past perfect) in the subordinate clause.

example_german: Falls es regnet, nehme ich den Schirm.
example_english: In case it rains, I'll take the umbrella.
